content.value_statement: Multi-agent systems are hard to design because coordination, context isolation, and failure modes interact. This skill gives practical patterns, tradeoffs, and examples for building reliable agent teams.
actual_capabilities: Explains supervisor, swarm, and hierarchical agent architecture patterns.
Shows how context isolation affects agent delegation and coordination.
Describes handoff protocols, weighted consensus, debate, and circuit breakers.
Compares framework approaches for LangGraph, AutoGen, and CrewAI.
Provides Python coordination utilities for messages, handoffs, voting, and failure recovery.
limitations: Does not install or run a complete multi-agent framework.
Examples need adaptation for production authentication, storage, and observability.
Assumes familiarity with agent tooling and basic Python concepts.
Does not replace framework documentation or a security review.

use_cases.title: Plan an Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Choose the best coordination pattern for a complex AI application before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Review Coordination Risks
use_cases.description: Identify bottlenecks, weak handoffs, consensus failures, and recovery gaps in an existing design.

use_cases.title: Compare Framework Options
use_cases.description: Map supervisor, swarm, and hierarchical designs onto LangGraph, AutoGen, or CrewAI concepts.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multi-agent-patterns to help me choose a multi-agent architecture for [project]. Compare supervisor, swarm, and hierarchical options.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Handoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multi-agent-patterns to design handoff protocols for [workflow]. Include state passed, completion signals, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multi-agent-patterns to review this agent architecture for context isolation, bottlenecks, consensus risks, and recovery gaps: [paste design].

prompt_templates.title: Create an Implementation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use multi-agent-patterns to create an implementation plan for [framework]. Include agent roles, state schema, consensus flow, tests, and observability.

output_examples.input: Design a research team that gathers sources, analyzes evidence, and writes a report.
output: Recommended pattern: supervisor, because the workflow has clear phases and quality gates.
Suggested agents: researcher, analyst, fact-checker, and writer.
Key safeguards: direct source forwarding, confidence scoring, and final validation before writing.

output_examples.input: Review a peer-to-peer agent swarm that keeps looping between specialists.
output: Primary issue: missing convergence constraints and no clear ownership of final decisions.
Recommended changes: add handoff limits, shared task state, and a completion authority.
Test focus: repeated handoffs, partial failures, and ambiguous requests.

output_examples.input: Compare LangGraph and AutoGen for a multi-agent customer support assistant.
output: LangGraph fits explicit routing, durable state, and testable workflow transitions.
AutoGen fits conversational collaboration and flexible group discussion.
Decision factor: choose based on control requirements, not framework popularity.

best_practices: Start with context isolation goals before assigning agent roles.
Use explicit handoff contracts, state boundaries, and completion criteria.
Test failure modes, loops, stale state, and weak consensus before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not create agents only to mirror an organization chart.
Do not let every agent see all shared history by default.
Do not use majority voting when agent expertise or confidence differs.

faq.question: Does this skill run multi-agent systems?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance, examples, and review criteria for designing multi-agent systems.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: No. The skill references external framework documentation, but it does not make network calls by itself.

faq.question: Can it help with production designs?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers handoffs, consensus, checkpointing, and failure recovery that production systems need.

faq.question: Does the skill write files?
faq.answer: The skill includes file coordination examples, but the skill content does not write files by itself.

faq.question: Is this useful for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, if they understand basic agent concepts. The templates help frame the first design decisions.
